newsitem.title: GERMANY: Munich Re says no plans to sell Salamander stake.
newsitem.headline: Munich Re says no plans to sell Salamander stake.

text.p: German insurance group Munich Re said on Monday it has no current plans to dispose of its 13.6 percent stake in German shoemaker Salamander AG.
Germany's Welt am Sonntag reported on Sunday that major shareholders in Salamander want to sell the shares due to the planned abolition of some taxes.
Deutsche Bank said earlier on Monday that it also had no current plans to sell its 10.7 percent stake.
Commerzbank AG, which owns 10.7 percent of Salamander, declined to comment.
German tax law had exempted shareholdings of between 10 and 25 percent from taxes on wealth, capital and capital trading.
But with the abolition and planned scrapping of the taxes, the holdings are losing their tax advantages, the paper said, citing informed sources.
Main shareholders in Salamander also include Austria's J.M. Voith AG with 15 percent and Victoria Lebensversicherungs AG with 12.3 percent.
Salamander shares ended last week at 201 marks ($118), down six, having rallied from a low of 149 marks in January.
